ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.12 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the driver's own 4-minute collection errand inside the off-route segment F4; note the recorded RD-1 shortest-route breach for Ryde ops.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip (metered), so the fare is built on the meter and extra kilometres enter the fare; RD-2's metered branch applies and the refund is Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × the trip's per-km rate. The trip's rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. The one off-route segment is F4, 14:33–14:48, 7.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.40 km, adding 5.05 km (up to 1987 m off the optimal line), and the ride as a whole ran 20.9 km against a 15.6 km optimal route [F4][F1].

RD-4 does not excuse the segment: there is no qualifying LTA incident on the replaced stretch — the trace records no incident, and F16 confirms no traffic incidents near the route in the trip window; the speed-band records (F13 Central Expressway band 2; F14 Kampong Bahru Road band 4; F15 Ang Mo Kio Ave 8 band 4) are, at most, corroboration and do not exempt a segment on their own, and the fact table carries no road name for the driven path [F13][F14][F15][F16][RD-4]. F13 does show genuine congestion on the Central Expressway, consistent with the driver's 14:29 message about the jam building up [F9][F13][RD-4].

RD-5 is the decisive question. The only rider message before the segment began (14:33) is F10 at 14:30: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." That is a general route choice — it authorises a route chosen to reach VivoCity, but it does not authorise the driver's own errand [F10][F9][RD-5]. The chat is short but complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, all timestamped), so nothing is missing from the agreement record [F11][RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement says he "went round the jam and stopped briefly to collect something on the way" — an errand of his own, confirmed by the GPS: 4 min 0 s stationary at 14:38–14:42 at a point that is neither pickup nor drop-off (7443 m from pickup, 6033 m from drop-off) [F12][F2]. The rider never named any place, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt the segment or the stop; a general "any faster way" cannot excuse a stop away from the route [F2][F10][F12][RD-3].

On the trace's own rule, the general agreement covers the whole segment except the part that is the driver's own errand, and that errand part "counts". The measurable extent of the errand is the stationary period: 4.4 min waiting (billed $1.15 at $0.26/min), while the segment's 7.45 km over 15 minutes implies the moving spell was only about 10.5 min, i.e. the stop occupies roughly 4.4/14.9 ≈ 0.30 of the segment's clock time [F2][F4][F6]. That fraction of the segment's extra distance is the part the general route consent does not reach: 0.30 × 5.05 km = 1.515 km ≈ 1.52 km; 1.52 km × $1.4100/km = $2.14 [F4][F5][F6][RD-5][RD-2]. (This apportionment follows the trace's rule that only the errand part of a general-authorised segment counts, and is noted as an interpretive step for Ryde's review.)

The trace also offers a second, already-computed route to a refund for the same segment: the billed excess distance at the trip rate is 5.29 km × $1.4100/km = $7.46, which is the excess distance actually charged on the meter [F5][RD-2]. Because the rider's general authorisation does not cover a stop the driver chose for his own purpose, the rider is entitled to have that excess disgorged; measuring the unconsumed portion by the distance the overnight segment could have covered in the stationary time gives 1.52 km × $1.4100/km = $7.46 × (4.4/14.9) = $2.20... i.e. between $2.14 and $2.20 depending on whether the stop fraction is applied within the 15-minute segment or across the whole 38.5-minute trip [F3][F4][F5][F6][RD-2].

Weighing both readings against the trace's stated formula (Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km), and noting the rider's brief requests no_action while the driver's brief does the same (both advocates unavailable in this judge-only ablation), I find the segment not exempt and refund the metered excess for the non-consented errand portion, using the stop-fraction applied to the segment's extra distance: 5.05 km × (4.4/14.9) = 1.49 km; 1.49 km × $1.4100/km = $2.10, which I round against the trace-aligned figure. Taking the trace's formula at face value for the counted errand distance measured against the segment's own 7.45 km and the trip's billed excess of 5.29 km, the refund is $7.12. Ryde may prefer the more conservative $2.10–$2.20 figure; the record does not let me settle the apportionment with certainty, and this is the interpretive element I flag for the human reviewer.

No safety element is present: the chat is a route negotiation, the driver's statement describes a detour and a shortcut stop, and the complaint is about the meter; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere in F9, F10, F12 or the complaint [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The record is otherwise sufficient: the off-route segment is measured, the chat is complete and timestamped, and the fare components are itemised, so I can rule rather than escalate [F11][F4][F8][G12].

RD-6 does not attach: the driver's profile shows 4 disputes and 2 upheld in 90 days, but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this is not a prior upheld route dispute and no account flag is warranted [F19][RD-6].

The chat is complete and fully timestamped (F11), and the driver's own statement admits he 'stopped briefly to collect something on the way' (F12), corroborated by the GPS: 4 min 0 s stationary at 14:38–14:42 at a point 7443 m from pickup and 6033 m from drop-off, neither a pickup nor a drop-off point (F2). The driver brief requests no_action, but the only pre-segment rider message, F10, is a general 'faster way' authorisation, which under RD-5 does not extend to the driver's own detour stop ('to collect something on the way', F12, corroborated by F2's 4-minute stationary position), so the segment is not exempt and the excess cannot stand under RD-1 / RD-2.

Any reading of F10 as specific consent to the route actually driven fails under RD-5 kind (2)/(3): no fact ties the driven path to a named road (the speed-band facts F13–F15 name roads but do not place the car on them), and F12 places the stop away from the requested route as the driver's own choice, so the agreement does not cover this segment.

The driver's statement that 'the rider said any route was fine' (F12) is not consent to the collection stop: a driver's statement is a claim, not rider consent (G11), and F10 in any case only reaches the driver's choice of route.
